scope: Source-grounded research and specification direction only; not implementation correctness, complete corpus audit, deployment approval or proof feasibility.
caveats: Native runtime corroboration is bounded to the 23 claims and 34 exact source ranges in studies/astra-runtime/claims.json. This vote does not independently validate other panel domains.
Availability joins and returned-status chains must retain all effect-relevant detached or late-branch duties; the candidate explicitly requires this.
Timeout and observed local failure remain distinct. An observed failed action can coexist with retained fees, prior-stage success and unresolved external consequences.

Conditional evidence readiness must remain separate from economic delivery. Evaluation of signatures/documents/proofs under the bound policy does not alone establish external delivery or document truth.
Target capability limits identify research and validation obligations; they must not silently narrow the controlling permissionless all-Midnight-DeFi language requirement.
No nearcore runtime tests, live protocol observations or Midnight/ZKIRv3 correspondence proofs were supplied by this review.
evidence_that_would_change_vote: A revised candidate requiring fresh original-user signatures or universal expiry checks for every authorized recovery continuation.
Pinned runtime evidence contradicting the independently inspected rollback, refund or returned-status semantics.
A requirements or implementation package that loses outstanding duties on failure, equates evidence readiness with delivery, or treats timeout as sufficient evidence of nonexecution.
An admission rule depending on maintainer approval, a fixed workflow-template allowlist, hosted solver credentials or an unbound execution-proof relation.
Concrete target ledger or proof-system evidence showing that a proposed construct cannot preserve its claimed semantics without an explicit conditional guarantee or rejected unsupported guarantee.
assessment: Candidate accurately incorporates receipt-local rollback exceptions, result-availability joins, persistent duties, staged authority and signed partial-settlement policies. Its precise conditional-settlement definition is coherent and does not claim NEAR itself implements arbitrary evidence combinations.
